post.description:
One authentication method per connector. `sasl`: SMTP AUTH on port 587 after STARTTLS; the username (`egc-…`) and a random password are generated and returned **once** in `credentials` (only an Argon2id hash is stored; rotate it if it is lost). `source_ip`: 1–20 networks (IPv4 ≥ /16, IPv6 ≥ /48) on the port 25 relay listener; networks must be publicly routable (private, loopback, link-local, shared, documentation, multicast and reserved ranges are `400` unless the deployment sets `SMTP_CONNECTOR_ALLOW_NON_PUBLIC_NETWORKS`) and may not overlap any network of any connector (`409 Network overlaps an existing connector network`). `client_certificate`: the SHA-256 fingerprint of the client certificate presented on port 25 (globally unique, `409`), optionally restricted to networks. `requireTls` (default true) only applies to `source_ip`; the other types always need TLS. At most `SMTP_CONNECTORS_MAX_PER_ORGANIZATION` (default 50) per organization (`409`). At most 20 per caller per minute (`429`). `source_ip` networks that overlap the shared sending ranges of Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace are `422 network_shared_provider` (`index`): connect the provider as a provider connection instead (step 8.2). `provider_relay` connectors cannot be created here.

**Warning:** never use `source_ip` connectors for shared-IP mail platforms such as Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace: every customer of that platform sends from the same addresses and could then send as your organization. Use `sasl` or `client_certificate` connectors for them.

networks.description: IPv4/IPv6 CIDR networks (a bare address is a single host); IPv4 prefix ≥ /16, IPv6 ≥ /48; host bits are cleared. Must be publicly routable (non-public ranges are refused unless SMTP_CONNECTOR_ALLOW_NON_PUBLIC_NETWORKS) and must not overlap any network of any other connector.

certificateFingerprintSha256.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the client certificate (hex, colons optional)

requireTls.description: Refuse sessions without STARTTLS (default true). Only source_ip connectors may set false.

providerConnectionId.description: provider_relay only: the id of the managing provider connection

get.description: Message metadata of your organization received in `[from, to)` (default the last 24 hours, at most API_MESSAGES_MAX_RANGE_DAYS days, default 31), newest first (`sort=-receivedAt`) or oldest first (`sort=receivedAt`), from the read replica (a few seconds behind the writer). **Search drivers (step 7.2).** The first present filter of `internetMessageId` > `sender` > `headerFrom` > `recipient` > `subject` > `senderDomain` > `recipientDomain` > `subjectPrefix` > `quarantineStatus` > `deliveryStatus` > `verdict` (exactly one value) drives the search: its index is read in time order, so a page with no other filter is exact (no short pages). Every other filter is a residual: with residuals each request examines at most API_LIST_SCAN_BUDGET_ROWS (default 5 000) entries of the driver’s index and may return a short or empty page with a `nextCursor`; with residuals only (no driver) the whole range is scanned that way. A message matched by several recipients, deliveries or quarantine entries is listed once. `subjectPrefix` reads at most API_MESSAGES_SEARCH_MAX_MATCHES (default 5 000) matching messages of the range: more is `422 message_search_too_broad` (type more, use the exact `subject` or narrow the range); a prefix search that takes longer than API_MESSAGES_SEARCH_TIMEOUT_MS is `503 message_search_timeout`. **Filter permissions.** `recipient`, `subject` and `subjectPrefix` require `message:reveal`, `deliveryStatus` requires `delivery:read`, `quarantineStatus` requires `quarantine:read` (`403 message_filter_forbidden` naming the filter and permission, before anything is read). Pages follow the v1 list contract: `{ data, nextCursor }`, no totals. When filters need non-indexed columns, each request examines at most API_LIST_SCAN_BUDGET_ROWS index entries (default 5 000), so a page may hold fewer rows than `limit` (even none) while `nextCursor` is set; follow `nextCursor` until it is null. The cursor is signed and bound to the filters, the sort, your organization and the first page’s time window: repeat the same filters (or omit `from`/`to`) with it, anything else is `400 cursor_invalid`. The cursor is also bound to the search driver: after a deploy that changes driver selection an old cursor is `400 cursor_invalid` once; restart the list. A search with `sender`, `headerFrom`, `recipient`, `internetMessageId`, `subject` or `subjectPrefix` is audited (`message.searched`, first page only; values only as SHA-256, subjects normalized first). Subjects and addresses are attacker-controlled text; bodies and attachments are never returned.

get.description: One entry per scan round (`round` = lifecycle round: 0 is the initial scan, each rescan adds one), newest first, cursor-paginated (at most 20 rounds per page): status, aggregate verdict (`clean`, `spam`, `suspicious`, `malicious`, `unknown`, `timeout`, `error`; null while running), reason codes, required engines, the deadline, the SPF/DKIM/DMARC/ARC results and per engine its final result (outcome, score, threshold, action, reason codes, symbols with bounded options, engine and settings versions) and every attempt (failed attempts are retried and listed with their error code). The `attachment` engine entry lists its per-attachment results (step 4.2): part index, sanitized filename, declared and detected type, size, SHA-256, verdict, reason codes, the ClamAV signature and versions, YARA rule matches, archive inspection counts and findings (by entry index path, never names), a known-hash hit and the sandbox submission. The content cache is shared across organizations, so its hit/miss outcome is never shown, and the `attachment` engine reports no durations and second-granular times. The `bec` engine entry (step 4.4) carries its explainable verdict: versions, deterministic and final verdict and score, thresholds, input states, the fired rules with structured evidence (span offsets, never text), applied and shadow AI assessments (no response hashes or durations) and feedback references; `scanId` of a round is the id the BEC feedback route takes. The `dlp` engine entry (step 4.5) carries its masked result (versions, verdict, action, coverage detail, category aggregates, findings with masked samples only, the policy match and applied exceptions as public ids, the evidence state) **only for callers also holding `dlp:read`**; otherwise `dlp` is null and only the standard engine fields are shown. Matched values are never shown here: decrypted evidence is only in the audited `GET /messages/{messageId}/scans/{scanId}/dlp-evidence`. Each round lists its stored risk scores in `risk` (step 5.1; revision 0 = the round, 1 = with the late sandbox result): score 0–1000, level, verdict, recommended action, hard blocks, contributions by signal and group, engine evidence, trust decision, explanation and every version (profile public ids only); `[]` while running. Step 5.1 recommends and does not enforce (policy, step 5.2, decides); the default weights and thresholds are not validated detection accuracy. Each round carries its stored policy evaluation in `policy` (step 5.2; null while not evaluated): disposition, decisive rule, actions with their status (`enforced`, `requested`, `recorded`, `not_applicable`), floor, recommendation, explanation and hashes (ids and codes only; the full list per message is `GET /messages/{messageId}/policy-evaluations`). From the read replica: a round that just completed may still show as running. Symbol options can contain addresses or URLs of the message; filenames are attacker-controlled text.

post.description: The stored subjects of up to 100 messages of your organization (`messageIds`, distinct; e.g. one explorer page), in request order. Unknown ids and ids of other organizations are omitted from `data` (they look the same). One audit row `message.revealed` per revealed message (`metadata: { fields: ["subject"], bulk: true }`). Requires `message:reveal` (user tokens and API keys holding it; platform override sessions are audited with the override). Values are read from the read replica, then one `message.revealed` audit row per revealed message (resource `message`/`<id>`; the fields and counts, never the values) is committed on the writer **before** the response is sent; if that write fails the answer is `503 service_unavailable` and no value is returned. `Cache-Control: no-store`: never cache, log or forward the response. Both reveal operations share one per-user/API-key limit of API_MESSAGES_REVEAL_PER_MINUTE (default 30) requests per minute (`429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After`). No Idempotency-Key (a read with an audit record, repeated calls are new reveals). Values are attacker-controlled text, returned as stored.

post.description: Fetches up to `limit` dead letters of `sourceQueue` (a work queue: `email.received`, `scan.spam`, `scan.url`, `scan.url.inspect`, `scan.url.results`, `scan.attachment`, `scan.bec`, `scan.dlp`, `scan.sandbox`, `scan.sandbox.submissions`, `scan.sandbox.results`, `email.policy.evaluate`, `email.delivery.pending`, `email.quarantine`, `email.archive`, `email.notifications`, `email.webhooks`, `ato.events`, `ato.mail`, `ato.responses`, `assistant.reports`; other queues are 400 `source_queue_not_replayable`) matching the optional filters, republishes each unchanged envelope to the source queue with fresh retry headers and a replay id, confirmed before the dead letter is removed. One replay at a time platform-wide (409 `replay_in_progress`); audited as `platform.dead_letters_replayed`. 503 `dead_letter_replay_unavailable` without RABBITMQ_OPS_URL or when the broker fails (the audit row then says `partial`).

parameters.description: Client-chosen key, 1-128 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`, unique per organization (case-sensitive). The first successful (2xx) response is stored for 24 hours: repeating the same request with the same key returns it again with the response header `Idempotency-Replayed: true` and changes nothing. The same key with a different request (body, path, operation or caller) is `422 idempotency_key_reused`. Errors (4xx) are not stored: fix the request and retry with the same key.

post.description: Streams the stored message of the organization to the Rspamd controller: `learn_spam` / `learn_ham` train the Bayes classifier (`already_learned` when Rspamd has learned it before or already classifies it that way), `fuzzy_add` / `fuzzy_delete` add or remove its fuzzy hashes with `fuzzyFlag` `spam` (flag 11, `EG_FUZZY_SPAM`) or `phishing` (flag 12, `EG_FUZZY_PHISH`). Bayes and fuzzy storage are shared by every organization, hence the platform permission. Learning does not rescan the message (use the rescan route). Audited as `scan_training.<operation>` with the outcome (never content); a successful call also adds the timeline event `scan.training`. 60 calls per caller per minute.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key, 1-128 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`, unique per organization (case-sensitive). The first successful (2xx) response is stored for 24 hours: repeating the same request with the same key returns it again with the response header `Idempotency-Replayed: true` and changes nothing. The same key with a different request (body, path, operation or caller) is `422 idempotency_key_reused`. Errors (4xx) are not stored: fix the request and retry with the same key.

post.description: Creates a `pending` admin job for messages received in the last `windowHours` (1-168) in the given `states` (default `scanned`, `scan_failed`, `quarantined`, `held_for_review`; never scanning, delivery or final states), optionally one organization, with at least one attachment and without a `malicious` attachment result in their current round (a `scan_failed` message always qualifies), at most `maxMessages` (default and maximum `ATTACHMENT_RESCAN_MAX_MESSAGES`). The email-worker executes it at a bounded rate: each message gets a new scan round on every engine. `estimatedMessages` counts the candidates now on the read replica (the worker selects on the writer as it goes). `dryRun: true` answers `200` with the count and writes nothing. Audited as `attachment_rescan.requested` (parameters only). 10 calls per caller per minute (shared by the rescan job routes).

parameters.description: Client-chosen key, 1-128 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`, unique per organization (case-sensitive). get.description: The only way to see matched values. An audit row `dlp_evidence.read` (actor, message, scan, match count; no content) is committed **before** the evidence is fetched and decrypted; a failure afterwards adds `dlp_evidence.read_failed` with the reason. The object (under `org/<org>/dlp-evidence/`) is checked against the recorded SHA-256 and size, its data key unwrapped with DLP_EVIDENCE_KEY and the document validated. Aadhaar numbers, private keys and secrets are masked even here; card numbers keep the first 6 and last 4 digits; card verification codes are never stored. Purged evidence answers `410 evidence_purged`, evidence past its retention `410 evidence_expired`. MFA-authenticated users only, 30 reads per user per minute; `Cache-Control: no-store`. Never cache, log or forward the response.

get.description: The DSL, input and evaluator versions, every field with its type, scope, operators, identity and AI flags and vocabulary, the operators, the nine actions, the dispositions (weakest first), the limits (P4 with this deployment’s organization bounds applied, plus `dryRunSampleMax` and `dryRunSamplesPerMinute`), the settings defaults and the platform default. Step 7.3 (ADR-0063) adds the presentation metadata a visual builder renders from: per field a `label`, `group`, `unit`, code `suggestions` and the `contexts` it may be used in; `fieldGroups`, `operatorDefinitions` (label, summary phrase, value shape, item kind and limits, negation), `actionDefinitions` (label, kind, disposition and parameter definitions), `quantifiers`, `scopeNouns`, `contextRules`, `weekdays`, `timeZones` (of the api runtime), `policyDirections` and `messageDirections`. Library data; no database access. The policy engine **enforces** the final disposition per recipient when rules are recipient-scoped (`recipientSplit`, step 5.3: ALLOW delivers; QUARANTINE and REQUIRE_APPROVAL create quarantine entries; REJECT discards the recipient) and the strictness floor (hard blocks, failures, the DLP binding and missing data are never weakened), plus TAG/WARN headers in a delivered copy; from step 5.3 the WARN body banner and URL_REWRITE are applied to the delivered copy after the scan when the message allows it (signed, encrypted or oversized messages record a `skipped_*` outcome instead). It **requests** ARCHIVE (performed by the archive-worker, step 8.1), ALERT and sender non-delivery notices (notification-worker). Quarantine release re-validates against the current policy (GET /quarantine/catalog); archiving and journaling are step 8.1.

strictOnly.description: Step 8.4 (D23): the field may only make a decision stricter (never in exceptions, ALLOW or override rules; `field_strict_only`) (always present since step 8.4; optional for older clients)

label.description: Plain-English label (unique; never the code name)

unit.description: Unit of an `int` field (`bytes`, `count`, `score`); null for other types

suggestions.description: Known codes for autocomplete of an open `codes` field (one without `values`); never a closed list (any reason code is accepted); null otherwise

contexts.description: Where the field may be used: every `when`; `exception` = rule `unless` and policy `exceptions` (not raw sender identity, not AI-derived, not strict-only); `relaxingWhen` = the `when` of ALLOW and override rules (not raw sender identity, not strict-only); `holdRule` = rules with REQUIRE_APPROVAL, QUARANTINE or REJECT (not AI-derived)

limits.description: The DSL limits (P4) with the organization bounds of this deployment applied, plus (step 7.3) `dryRunSampleMax` (POLICY_DRY_RUN_SAMPLE_MAX) and `dryRunSamplesPerMinute` (POLICY_SAMPLE_DRY_RUNS_PER_MINUTE)

post.description: Evaluates synthetic facts (every field optional with documented defaults; `evaluationTime` defaults to the request time) against `target` with the same evaluator the policy-engine runs (floor and platform default included) and returns the full result: disposition, decisive rule, actions with applicability, delivery header edits, trace, floor, recommendation, override and clamps, explanation and hashes. The synthetic risk facts are trusted for the test only. Active policies and versions are read from the read replica. **Writes nothing**: no evaluation row, no audit row, no event. The policy engine **enforces** the final disposition per recipient when rules are recipient-scoped (`recipientSplit`, step 5.3: ALLOW delivers; QUARANTINE and REQUIRE_APPROVAL create quarantine entries; REJECT discards the recipient) and the strictness floor (hard blocks, failures, the DLP binding and missing data are never weakened), plus TAG/WARN headers in a delivered copy; from step 5.3 the WARN body banner and URL_REWRITE are applied to the delivered copy after the scan when the message allows it (signed, encrypted or oversized messages record a `skipped_*` outcome instead). It **requests** ARCHIVE (performed by the archive-worker, step 8.1), ALERT and sender non-delivery notices (notification-worker). Quarantine release re-validates against the current policy (GET /quarantine/catalog); archiving and journaling are step 8.1.

target.description: `active`: the organization’s active policies now (replica); `platform`: the platform default alone (the tenant settings apply); `{ policyId, versionNo }`: the active policies with that version (draft or published) in place of the policy’s active version (added when the policy is not active); `{ definition }`: an unsaved definition, validated like a draft (`400 policy_definition_invalid`), added to the active policies as policy `00000000-0000-7000-8000-000000000000` version 1

definition.description: A `policy-dsl/1` document: `{ dslVersion, direction, priority, rules[], exceptions? }` (see `GET /policies/catalog` and docs/architecture/policy-dsl.md)

facts.description: Synthetic facts (P23); every field optional with documented defaults; `evaluationTime` defaults to the request time; `resolveDirectory: true` resolves department and user memberships of the facts’ addresses from the directory

recipientSplit.description: Step 5.3 (Q4): true when the recipients were evaluated one by one and their dispositions differ (recipient-scoped rules, `recipientSplit` setting on, ≤ 200 recipients)

recipientDecisions.description: Per-recipient decisions (rcptSeq, disposition, source, decisive rule, ≤ 8 reason codes); empty when the message was not evaluated per recipient (no recipient-scoped rule, one recipient, setting off, truncated or too many recipients)

lifecycleDisposition.description: The disposition the message as a whole receives (Q4.4, Q5): the strictest per-recipient disposition when uniform; with a split, the message follows its allowed recipients

invalidVersions.description: Versions of the snapshot the current DSL no longer accepts (excluded)

post.description: Re-evaluates the newest stored evaluation of each message of your organization (rounds with a scan) whose `receivedAt` is in [`sample.from`, `sample.to`) (default: the last 7 days; at most POLICY_HISTORY_MAX_RANGE_DAYS), optionally of one `direction`, newest first, against `target` (`active`, `platform`, `{ policyId, versionNo }` or an inline `{ definition }`, as `POST /policies/test`). The target snapshot is compiled once; each round’s facts are read from the read replica exactly as `POST /messages/{messageId}/scans/{scanId}/policy/dry-run` reads them, one round after the other. Bounds: `sample.limit` 1..POLICY_DRY_RUN_SAMPLE_MAX (default 25; above → `400`), at most `limit × 4` stored rows read, and POLICY_DRY_RUN_DEADLINE_MS (on expiry the evaluated prefix is returned with `truncated: true`). Each item compares the stored and the recomputed message-level disposition and decisive rule (`dispositionChanged`, `decisiveChanged`); the summary counts them and the transitions. Items carry message public ids, times, enums, rule ids and counts only, never subjects, addresses or content. **Writes nothing**: no evaluation row, no audit row, no event, no idempotency record. Requires `policy:manage` and `message:read`; class `expensive` plus POLICY_SAMPLE_DRY_RUNS_PER_MINUTE per user or API key (`429 rate_limited`, `scope: route`). The JSON body limit of this route is 327680 bytes (the DSL’s 262 144-byte document limit plus 64 KiB for the rest of the request): every definition the DSL accepts fits; a larger body is answered `413 payload_too_large` before it reaches the route. The policy engine **enforces** the final disposition per recipient when rules are recipient-scoped (`recipientSplit`, step 5.3: ALLOW delivers; QUARANTINE and REQUIRE_APPROVAL create quarantine entries; REJECT discards the recipient) and the strictness floor (hard blocks, failures, the DLP binding and missing data are never weakened), plus TAG/WARN headers in a delivered copy; from step 5.3 the WARN body banner and URL_REWRITE are applied to the delivered copy after the scan when the message allows it (signed, encrypted or oversized messages record a `skipped_*` outcome instead). It **requests** ARCHIVE (performed by the archive-worker, step 8.1), ALERT and sender non-delivery notices (notification-worker). Quarantine release re-validates against the current policy (GET /quarantine/catalog); archiving and journaling are step 8.1.

parameters.description: Client-chosen key, 1-128 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`, unique per organization (case-sensitive). The first successful (2xx) response is stored for 24 hours: repeating the same request with the same key returns it again with the response header `Idempotency-Replayed: true` and changes nothing. The same key with a different request (body, path, operation or caller) is `422 idempotency_key_reused`. Errors (4xx) are not stored: fix the request and retry with the same key.

get.description: Every stored policy evaluation of a message of the organization, newest round first (a parse-failure evaluation has no scan): disposition, final verdict and action, decisive source/policy/rule, actions with applicability and the status the engine achieved (`enforced`, `requested`, `recorded`, `not_applicable`), delivery header edits, trace, floor, recommendation, override and clamps, explanation, delivered object, versions, generation and hashes. Never addresses or message content. From the read replica. The policy engine **enforces** the final disposition per recipient when rules are recipient-scoped (`recipientSplit`, step 5.3: ALLOW delivers; QUARANTINE and REQUIRE_APPROVAL create quarantine entries; REJECT discards the recipient) and the strictness floor (hard blocks, failures, the DLP binding and missing data are never weakened), plus TAG/WARN headers in a delivered copy; from step 5.3 the WARN body banner and URL_REWRITE are applied to the delivered copy after the scan when the message allows it (signed, encrypted or oversized messages record a `skipped_*` outcome instead). It **requests** ARCHIVE (performed by the archive-worker, step 8.1), ALERT and sender non-delivery notices (notification-worker). Quarantine release re-validates against the current policy (GET /quarantine/catalog); archiving and journaling are step 8.1.

The cursor is bound to the filters (`400 quarantine_cursor_invalid` with other filters). `subject` is returned only to holders of `quarantine:preview`. `recipient` is in clear only for holders of a quarantine decision permission (`quarantine:release`, `quarantine:approve`, `quarantine:reject`, `quarantine:delete`, `quarantine:request_release`, `quarantine:manage`) or `message:reveal`; for every other caller it is masked (`f***@example.com`) and `recipientMasked` is true (step 7.2). The exact `recipient` filter needs the same permissions (a caller who reads recipients masked gets `403 quarantine_filter_forbidden`: the search would confirm the masked address; ADR-0062). Read replica: an entry just created may be missing for the replication lag. Audited as `quarantine.searched` (filter hash and count only).

post.description: Registers an endpoint for the listed event types (1-10 of the catalogue, no wildcard) with optional filters (`directions`, `domainIds` of your domains, `minSeverity`, `verdicts`). The URL must be absolute `https` (≤ 2048, no userinfo or fragment, a port of WEBHOOK_ALLOWED_PORTS) and its host must not be a private, loopback, link-local, metadata or other special-purpose address or one of the platform’s own hosts (`422 webhook_url_not_allowed` with `reason`). DNS is not resolved here: the delivery worker checks every resolved address on every attempt. Needs the plan feature `webhooks` (`403 webhooks_not_enabled`); at most WEBHOOK_MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS_PER_ORG live subscriptions (`409 webhook_limit_reached`). Returns `201` with the webhook and its signing `secret`. Requires the Idempotency-Key header (transactional: the change, its audit row and the stored response commit together; rate class `sensitive`). The secret is shown ONLY in this response: the stored response under the key is the same body with `secret: null`, so repeating the request with the same key returns it with `Idempotency-Replayed: true` and `secret: null` (ADR-0057). A client that lost the original response rotates the secret (with a new key). Audited `webhook.created` (`urlHost` and `urlSha256`, never the URL or the secret).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key, 1-128 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`, unique per organization (case-sensitive). The first successful (2xx) response is stored for 24 hours: repeating the same request with the same key returns it again with the response header `Idempotency-Replayed: true` and changes nothing. The same key with a different request (body, path, operation or caller) is `422 idempotency_key_reused`. Errors (4xx) are not stored: fix the request and retry with the same key.

get.description: Metadata search of your organization’s archive (OpenSearch, through your tenant alias; no bodies, no attachment content). `from` and `to` are required (at most ARCHIVE_SEARCH_MAX_RANGE_DAYS, `400 archive_search_range_invalid`). Filters that would confirm a masked value — `recipient`, `subject`, `custodian` — need `message:reveal`; `holdId` needs `archive:legal_hold` or `ediscovery:manage` (`403 archive_filter_forbidden`, `filter`, before any query). Results are masked for every caller (subjects null, recipients `f***@example.com`; sender side and attachment names in clear); clear values only through the audited reveal. No totals; `nextCursor` (v1, `archive_messages`) is bound to the filters, the range and the sort. The response header `X-EG-Index-Lag-Seconds` gives the age of your oldest change not yet indexed. Step 8.6: `ingestSource` (`gateway`, `journal_intake`) filters on where a copy came from; items carry `ingestSources`. Search unavailable or not configured: `503 archive_search_unavailable` (detail and content routes keep working). The first page is audited `archive.searched` (filter names and hashes, never values). Rate class `expensive`.

profiles.title: Account takeover telemetry (read-only)
profiles.description: Reads sign-in logs, risk detections, consent audits, Exchange mailbox audit and inbox rules for account takeover detection. Grants no write permission.

profiles.title: Account takeover response
profiles.description: Revokes sessions, disables accounts, requires a password change and disables or deletes inbox rules, each only after an approved response action.

profiles.title: Account takeover response (extended, high privilege)
profiles.description: Adds users to the tenant's MFA enforcement group and revokes OAuth permission grants. DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All is a very powerful permission; grant it only if OAuth grant revocation is wanted.

streams.notes: Graph v1.0 auditLogs/signIns (interactive sign-ins). Needs Entra ID P1 or P2.
Graph v1.0 identityProtection/riskDetections. Without Entra ID P2 the risk level is hidden and such detections carry no level.
Graph v1.0 auditLogs/directoryAudits consent activities; publisher verification is read from the service principal when the directory read permission is granted.

Office 365 Management Activity API Audit.Exchange (allow-listed operations only) plus targeted and weekly inbox rule reads through Graph when MailboxSettings.Read is granted (otherwise rule traits come from the audit parameter names). Content is kept 7 days by the provider.
Set-Mailbox forwarding parameters and forwarding inbox rules from the mailbox audit feed.
Mailbox permission, send-as and send-on-behalf changes from the mailbox audit feed.
Token risk detection types of the risk detections feed.

actions.notes: POST users/{id}/revokeSignInSessions; the 2xx answer is the effect.
Adds the user to the tenant-designated security group targeted by the customer's own Conditional Access policy; never edits Conditional Access.

Sets passwordProfile.forceChangePasswordNextSignIn (not readable back; confirmed by the 2xx answer). Cloud-only users only; users synchronized from on-premises fail with on_premises_managed. Privileged users may need a directory role for the app.
accountEnabled = false, confirmed by read-back; rollback re-enables only an account the gateway disabled.
Disables (default) or deletes inbox rules. Mailbox-level forwarding (Set-Mailbox) cannot be changed through Graph: unsupported, manual step in Exchange admin. Rollback only in disable mode.
Deletes the user's delegated permission grants of the application, confirmed by a re-list.

licences.title: Unified audit logging enabled
licences.enables: Exchange mailbox audit through the Office 365 Management Activity API

notes: Each profile is its own multi-tenant app with a disjoint permission set, consented separately.
Some writes need an Entra directory role for the app (for example password-profile updates of privileged users); the action then fails with missing_privileged_role.

profiles.title: Account takeover telemetry
profiles.description: Reads login and token audit reports, the user directory and Gmail forwarding, filter and delegate settings. Gmail has no read-only settings scope: gmail.settings.basic technically allows filter changes, but the telemetry adapter only reads.

profiles.title: Account takeover response
profiles.description: Signs users out, revokes OAuth tokens, suspends users, requires a password change, deletes forwarding filters and disables auto-forwarding, each only after an approved response action.

profiles.title: Account takeover response (extended)
profiles.description: Moves users to the tenant-designated organizational unit that enforces 2-Step Verification.

streams.notes: Admin SDK Reports activities.list application login.
Suspicious login and account hijack events of the login report.
Admin SDK Reports application token, event authorize.
Gmail filters from the settings snapshot sweep; mailbox access events are not available.
Gmail settings snapshot sweep (auto-forwarding, filters, delegates) per user through domain-wide delegation; detects state, not who changed it.
Accepted Gmail delegates from the settings snapshot sweep.
Not offered: Google exposes no session or token anomaly events through supported APIs.

actions.notes: Directory users.signOut (every web and device session), then every OAuth token of the user is revoked (tokens.delete), as Entra session revocation also invalidates refresh tokens; confirmed when a re-list shows no token. Applications must be authorized again by the user.
Moves the user to the tenant-designated organizational unit with 2-Step Verification enforced (every policy of that unit applies); rollback restores the previous unit.
suspended = true, confirmed by read-back; rollback unsuspends only a user the gateway suspended.

Disables auto-forwarding (gmail.settings.sharing) or deletes forwarding filters (gmail.settings.basic), impersonating the mailbox owner; confirmed by read-back; cannot be rolled back (the gateway keeps no forwarding address or filter definition).
Directory tokens.delete for the application's client id, confirmed by a re-list.

notes: Each profile is its own service account with domain-wide delegation, authorized separately.
Admin SDK calls impersonate the delegated administrator of the grant; Gmail settings calls impersonate each user.
Every action first reads the directory user (admin.directory.user) to check that the address is in a provider-verified linked domain.
Actions on super administrators need a super-administrator delegated admin; otherwise they fail with missing_privileged_role.

post.description: Runs one turn: your `message` (1..ASSISTANT_USER_MESSAGE_MAX_CHARS characters, `413 payload_too_large` beyond) goes to the configured AI provider with the catalogue of the tools you may use; the model may call tools, each one existing `/api/v1` operation executed with YOUR credential through the api’s own pipeline (same permissions, tenant, MFA, rate limits and audit as the portal), recorded and audited (`assistant.tool_executed` / `assistant.tool_denied`). A write call never runs inside a turn: it becomes a confirmation (`pending_confirmation`) that runs only through `POST /assistant/confirmations/{id}/confirm`; outcomes of earlier confirmations are told to the model at the start of the next turn. Limits per turn: ASSISTANT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS model calls, ASSISTANT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS_PER_TURN tool calls, ASSISTANT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS output tokens, ASSISTANT_TURN_DEADLINE_MS. Refusals before the answer starts are JSON errors: availability (`503 assistant_disabled`, `403 assistant_not_enabled`, `403 assistant_tenant_disabled`, `503 assistant_provider_unavailable`, `429 assistant_budget_exhausted` with `scope`), ASSISTANT_TURNS_PER_USER_PER_MINUTE (`429 rate_limited`), the per-process concurrency (`503 assistant_busy`) and one running turn per conversation (`409 assistant_turn_in_progress`). The same `clientTurnId` again replays a finished turn (`409` while it runs). Rate class `expensive`. With `accept: text/event-stream` the answer is `assistant-stream/1` (Server-Sent Events: `event:` name + one `data:` JSON line; a `: heartbeat` comment every 15 s): `turn.started { turnId, conversationId, seq }` (flushed before the first model call), then any interleaving of `text.delta { text }`, `tool.started { executionId, tool, title }`, `tool.completed { executionId, status, decision, card }` (status `pending_confirmation` for a write proposal, immediately followed by `confirmation.required { confirmation, token }`: the confirmation card and its single-use token, keep it in memory only) and `tool.denied { executionId, tool, decision, message }`, then exactly one of `turn.completed { turnId, status, usage: { inputTokens, outputTokens }, messageId }` or `turn.failed { turnId, code, message }` (codes `assistant_session_expired`, `assistant_turn_limit`, `assistant_refused`, `assistant_provider_error`, `assistant_internal_error`). Headers `cache-control: no-store` and `x-accel-buffering: no`. Otherwise the JSON `{ turn, message, executions, confirmations }` after the turn ended (`confirmations[].token` is null on a replay). Users only (API keys `403 user_required`); the tenant always comes from your session.

post.description: Runs the stored request of a pending proposal, exactly as the card showed it, through the api’s own pipeline with YOUR credential (permissions, tenant, MFA, rate limits, validation, CAS, approvals and audit apply as in the portal) with `Idempotency-Key` = the confirmation id where the operation takes one. Send the single-use `token` of the `confirmation.required` event (or the turn’s `confirmations[]`) and the `actionDigest` the card showed; high-risk actions also need `reauth` (`password`, and `totpCode` with MFA) unless this session re-authenticated an assistant confirmation within ASSISTANT_REAUTH_WINDOW_SECONDS. Checks in order: own confirmation (`404`), same sign-in session (`403 assistant_confirmation_session_mismatch`), still pending (`409 assistant_confirmation_not_pending` with `status`), not expired (`410 assistant_confirmation_expired`), the token (`403 assistant_confirmation_token_invalid`; the fifth wrong token cancels the confirmation), the digest (`409 assistant_confirmation_digest_mismatch`), the tool still enabled (`409 assistant_confirmation_tool_changed`; also when the effective risk recomputed from the stored arguments differs from the stored one) and permitted (`403 forbidden`), the proposal guards (`403 assistant_action_not_allowed`: no change to your own account, roles, status, MFA or sessions, nor to the assistant’s own enablement or who may configure it, through chat), the assistant available, re-authentication (`401 assistant_reauth_required`, `401 assistant_reauth_failed` with `reason`; failures count toward the login lockout), no turn running in the conversation (`409 assistant_turn_in_progress`), then the target is read again and any change since the proposal refuses (`409 assistant_confirmation_state_changed`) and the proposal guards that need the target are evaluated on it again (`403 assistant_action_not_allowed`). A write the operation itself refuses is a `200` with `confirmation.status = failed` and the execution’s error card; `202` approval answers are `executed`. The assistant learns the outcome at the start of its next turn. Rate class `sensitive`. A confirmation belongs to the user, organization (and platform override) and sign-in session that the assistant proposed it in; another user’s or organization’s answers `404`. Users only (API keys `403 user_required`); the tenant always comes from your session.

info.title: Email Security Gateway API
info.description:
Control-plane API of the Email Security Gateway. Every business route is under `/api/v1` (ADR-0015, ADR-0053); nothing else is public. Probes (`/health/live`, `/health/ready`) and the Prometheus scrape (`/metrics`) are internal endpoints of the api port, never routed by the Ingress and not part of this document; this document itself (`/docs`, `/docs-json`) is served outside production only.

**Authentication.** A bearer access token (`Authorization: Bearer <JWT>`, from `POST /api/v1/auth/login`) or, where an operation lists the `api-key` scheme, an organization API key (`X-API-Key`). The organization is always the caller’s (the token or key), never a header or a body field; another tenant’s resource answers `404`. `x-eg-permissions` names the permission(s) each operation requires.

**Conventions (ADR-0050).** Resources are plural kebab-case nouns; a single resource is returned bare, a collection as `{ "data": [...], "nextCursor": string | null }` (the quarantine lists of step 5.3 keep `items`). Every error is `{ statusCode, error, code, message, correlationId, requestId, ... }` with a stable snake_case `code`; every response carries `X-Request-Id` (server-minted) and `x-correlation-id`. Request bodies and query strings are strict: an unknown field is `400 validation_failed`.

**Lists (ADR-0051).** `limit` (1-100, default 25) and `cursor`; keyset order, no totals, no offsets. Lists added in 6.1 (`x-eg-cursor: v1`) use signed cursors bound to the organization, the filters and the sort (`400 cursor_invalid` otherwise); earlier lists keep their unsigned `v0` cursors. A page may be short, even empty, while `nextCursor` is not null (scan budget): follow `nextCursor` until it is null. Filters are `field=value`, `field=a,b` and `field.gte=` / `.lte=` / `.gt=` / `.lt=`; `sort=-receivedAt` style.

**Rate limits and idempotency (ADR-0052).** Authenticated requests are limited per user or API key and per organization (60 s windows; `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset`); `x-eg-rate-class: sensitive | expensive` operations have their own tighter bucket. `429 rate_limited` carries `scope` and `Retry-After`; when the limiter store is down the API answers `503` (fail closed). Operations with `x-eg-idempotency` require an `Idempotency-Key` header (`required`: exactly once with the effect; `legacy`: the reservation interceptor, at most once per key); replays carry `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. Responses that contain a secret (`x-eg-returns-secret`) are never stored and take no key, except the two webhook secret routes (`x-eg-secret-replay: redacted`, ADR-0057): they require a key, store the response with `secret: null` and return the secret only in the original response.

**Integration surfaces today.** Organization API keys (`/api/v1/api-keys`, scoped to tenant permissions) for this API, SMTP connectors (`/api/v1/smtp-connectors`) for outbound relay from customer systems, and signed webhooks (`/api/v1/webhooks`, step 6.2) for mail, threat, quarantine and domain events.

**Not offered, by design.** `delivery_routes` management: no service reads that table (inbound destinations are `/domains/{id}/destinations`, outbound relay is SMTP connectors), so a management API would change nothing. Tenant-managed threat indicators and IP/domain/URL reputation: no engine reads tenant rows; tenants can look up the platform data the engines use (`GET /threat-intelligence/lookup`) and keep their own allow-lists as BEC trusted senders, DLP exceptions and policy conditions. Prices, invoices and payments: no such data exists (`GET /billing/plan` says `pricing: null`).

**Deferred to later steps.** Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace connectors: step 8.2. Deployment manager: step 8.3. Admin-portal screens (webhooks, delivery history, preferences): steps 7.x.

tags.description: Step 1.3: login events. Step 6.1: the organization’s audit log (`GET /audit/logs`, `audit:read`, signed cursors, bounded range, the search itself audited).

tags.name: organizations
tags.description: Step 1.2: organizations, settings, features, limits (incl. the per-tenant API rate limit `api_requests_per_minute`), usage and the deletion workflow.

tags.name: domains
tags.description: Steps 2.1-2.3: domains, DNS verification and records, DKIM rotation, the inbound recipient registry and the inbound destination servers.

tags.name: smtp-connectors
tags.description: Step 2.2: outbound SMTP relay connectors (an integration surface of today); secrets shown once.

tags.name: deliveries
tags.description: Step 2.3: per-message delivery status, delivery events and the delivery list.

tags.name: messages
tags.description: Step 3.3: lifecycle, history, rescan, release. Step 4.1: scan results. Step 6.1: the message list (replica, signed cursors, scan budget), detail and recipients. Step 7.2: the Email Explorer search (index drivers for sender, From, recipient, subject, Message-ID, domains, delivery and quarantine states; budgeted residual filters; the capped subject prefix; filter-level permissions), the stored headers, and sensitive metadata masked for every caller (subjects, recipient addresses, To/Cc/Subject header values) with the audited `message:reveal` operations. Message content and S3 keys are never returned.

tags.name: scan-settings
tags.description: Step 4.1: per-organization engine settings (including URL protection).

tags.name: attachments
tags.description: Step 6.1: attachment metadata and verdicts of a message and the SHA-256 search; never content (downloads only through quarantine download grants, step 5.3).

tags.name: url-protection
tags.description: Step 6.1: the URLs of a message with their verdicts and rewrite status, and the time-of-click events (step 4.3 click-service data). Settings are `/scan-settings/url`.

tags.name: recipients
tags.description: Step 6.1: the recipient suppression list the outbound path enforces (bounces, complaints, manual and unsubscribe entries); create and delete need an Idempotency-Key.

tags.name: bec
tags.description: Step 4.4: BEC executives, vendors, trusted senders, feedback.

tags.name: dlp
tags.description: Step 4.5: DLP policies, rules, exceptions, patterns, dictionaries, compliance packs, incidents and the audited evidence routes.

tags.name: risk-scoring
tags.description: Step 5.1: versioned risk profiles, publish, activate, reset and dry-runs.

tags.name: policies
tags.description: Step 5.2: policies, versions, publish and activation, tests and dry-runs, settings and execution history.

tags.name: departments
tags.description: Step 5.2: departments and members used by policies.

tags.name: quarantine
tags.description: Step 5.3: quarantine search, preview, download grants, release with re-validation, approvals, end-user self-service and settings.

tags.name: reports
tags.description: Step 6.1: traffic, threat and URL-click aggregates computed on the replica over bounded ranges, cached per organization (`503 report_timeout` instead of an overloaded replica). Step 7.1: the threats `outcomes` matrix and the delivery, processing (time to verdict) and top attacked domains reports of the admin dashboard.

tags.name: usage
tags.description: Step 6.1: the caller’s organization usage (same data as step 1.2’s route).

tags.name: billing
tags.description: Step 6.1: the plan, effective entitlements and monthly metered quantities from recorded data. No prices, invoices or payments exist (`pricing: null`).

tags.name: threat-intelligence
tags.description: Step 6.1: look up a hash, URL, domain or IP in the platform threat data the engines use (audited, expensive class). Tenant-managed indicators are not offered.

tags.name: webhooks
tags.description: Step 6.2: signed webhook subscriptions (HMAC-SHA256 `EG-Signature`, secret shown once, rotation with overlap), the event catalogue, delivery history with attempts, single and time-range replay, test pings. `webhook:read` / `webhook:manage`; needs the plan feature `webhooks`. Not offered: events for SMTP-time refusals, per-recipient deliveries, URL clicks, DLP incidents and archive actions, connector events (8.2), payload version 2, custom headers or mTLS, back-fill of past events; portal screens: 7.x.

tags.name: notifications
tags.description: Step 6.2: tenant security-alert settings (threat detected, DNS record failures, webhook disabled: enabled, severity, throttle windows) and the caller’s own notification preferences (opt-outs, quarantine digest). E-mail only; SMS, chat and push channels are not offered; portal screens: 7.x.

tags.name: saved-views
tags.description: Step 7.2: the caller’s saved Email Explorer views (filters, sort, range, columns), per user and organization, `message:read`, members only (no API keys or platform overrides). Shared or organization-wide views are not offered.

tags.name: journaling
tags.description: Step 8.6: the Journaling area (capture). The journaling half of the archive settings (the same row and `rowVersion` as `/archive/settings`: enabled, directions, categories, scope, policy-rule archiving, journal intake scanning), the journaling status, and journal-only intake: per-source intake addresses `journal-<token>@<intake domain>` for Microsoft 365 / on-premises Exchange journal reports, Google Workspace copies and SMTP BCC copies (derived, never stored; shown once, masked afterwards, audited reveal and rotation with overlap), kind-specific sender rules (the bound step 8.2 connection or registered networks), the computed setup wizard, customer guides (JSON or Markdown) and attestations. `journal:read` / `journal:manage` (ADR-0089). Capture issues and the settings operations of the archive tag are listed here too. Intake mail is archived, never delivered, and never appears in the Email Explorer, reports or usage counts of filtered mail. Not offered: import of historical mail (PST, mbox, provider export).

tags.name: archive
tags.description: Step 8.1: journaling and compliance archiving. Archive settings (journal directions, categories, scope, immutability, access switches), retention policies, per-tenant encryption key versions and audited rotation, capture issues, the disposal log, the export signing keys, metadata search over the tenant's OpenSearch alias (masked like the Email Explorer; reveal through the audited `message:reveal`), detail, journal report, frozen scan results, the sanitized preview and single-use re-authorized downloads (customer-only: never under a platform override), and disposal of records under review. Every read of archived content is audited before it is returned. Not offered: content (body) search, per-attachment downloads, backfill of mail received before journaling was enabled, shortening retention of existing records, re-wrapping record keys after a rotation (8.x / 10.x). Step 8.6 (ADR-0089): record detail, journal, security and reveal need `archive:search` (organization admins hold no archive access by default; the `compliance_officer` role does), the settings are authorized per changed path, search filters on `ingestSource` and records list their copy sources and merged copies.

tags.name: ediscovery
tags.description: Step 8.1: eDiscovery cases with custodians, case-scoped legal holds, worker-run case searches verified against MySQL with explicit completeness flags, review tags, and bounded encrypted EML exports with a signed chain-of-custody manifest (Ed25519, public keys at `GET /archive/export-signing-keys`) downloaded through single-use re-authorized grants. Organization-wide legal hold views under `/legal-holds`. Not offered: per-case access lists, API-key retrieval of exports, PST/MBOX exports, split exports above the bounds.

tags.name: ato
tags.description: Step 8.4: account takeover detection (off by default; a platform operator enables the plan feature `ato_detection` per organization). Overview and attention counts, monitored accounts (mailboxes, gateway users, SMTP connectors) with explainable risk scores, signals, authentication events, activity and score history, analyst overrides, protection and trusted contexts, the ATO evidence of incidents, response actions with approvals (four eyes, MFA) and rollback, SMTP sending restrictions and authentication blocks, settings and the rule catalogue. Step 8.5: identity-provider integrations (Microsoft Entra ID / Microsoft 365, Google Workspace) bound to step 8.2 connections (settings, health, streams, backfill, pause, removal) and the mailbox state of an account (forwarding, inbox rules, delegates) with its priority refresh. `ato:read`, `ato:manage`, `ato:respond`, `ato:configure`. Not offered: platform-wide views across tenants.

tags.name: incidents
tags.description: Step 8.4: security incidents shared by account takeover and (later) advanced threat protection: list, manual creation, detail with the category detail, status transitions (open, investigating, confirmed, false positive, mitigated, resolved), assignment, notes, timeline, linked messages and the audited report. Access is per category: a category’s incidents need its read/manage permission (account takeover: `ato:read`/`ato:manage`); others answer 404. Receivers of the `security.incident.*` webhooks ignore unknown categories.

tags.name: provider-connections
tags.description: Step 8.2: Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace connections. The catalogue of read-only permission profiles, connections with grants (Microsoft admin consent with a single-use state, Google domain-wide delegation, or encrypted customer credentials that are never returned), linked TXT-verified domains, the server-computed setup wizard, preview → impact token → apply for every gateway-side mail-flow change (inbound destinations, the provider relay connector, outbound activation, proof policy, suspension, disconnection), attestations of customer-side steps, validation runs with single-use probe addresses, health, and customer-specific setup guides (JSON or Markdown). The gateway never writes to a customer tenant and the api never calls Microsoft or Google (provider traffic runs in the integration-worker). Not offered: automatic configuration of Exchange Online or Gmail, customer certificate credentials, automatic outbound suspension on health.

tags.name: assistant
tags.description: Step AI-1: the AI assistant (docs/plan/steps/28-ai-chat-management.md, ADR-0091–0094). Status, organization settings (enable with the external-processing acknowledgement, daily token budget, content retention), usage, your tool catalogue, your conversations and messages, turns answered as JSON or as the `assistant-stream/1` event stream, cancellation, stored tool executions and their next pages. Every tool is an existing `/api/v1` operation executed with your own credential through this API (same permissions, tenant, MFA, rate limits and audit as the portal). Step AI-2 (docs/plan/steps/29-ai-chat-confirmations-mail-writes.md, ADR-0093): the assistant only PROPOSES writes; a write runs when you confirm its confirmation card (`POST /assistant/confirmations/{id}/confirm` with the single-use token, the card’s digest and, for high risk, re-authentication). Users only; these routes are never tools themselves.

tags.name: platform
tags.description: Platform staff only: overrides (1.3), dead letters (3.2), scan training (4.1), threat hashes and attachment rescans (4.2), threat indicators (4.3), cross-tenant audit log (6.1, users with MFA, audited).

ErrorBody.description: Every error of the API (step 6.1 D1). `code` is a stable snake_case machine code; `message` is a string, or a list of `"<path>: <issue>"` strings for validation errors. Coded errors may add detail fields (ids, states, versions, codes; never content).

code.description: `validation_failed` (unknown fields included), or a specific code such as `cursor_invalid`, `idempotency_key_required`, `idempotency_key_invalid`

X-Request-Id.description: Server-minted id of this request (UUID); quote it when reporting a problem

X-Correlation-Id.description: The caller-supplied x-correlation-id if well formed, otherwise a new one

RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests allowed in the current 60 s window of the most restrictive limit

Idempotency-Replayed.description: `true` when the stored response of an earlier request with the same key is returned
